messages:
mara: draft idea — build a compact benchmark story that centers on 'predictable inference economics' rather than raw fastest-is-best. focus on latency distributions + unit cost tradeoffs. short writeup and 2–3 visuals.

alex: love this. do you mean show avg latency + 95/99 tail + tokens-per-dollar?

mara: yes. three panels: 1) latency CDF (avg vs 95/99), 2) cost per 1k tokens across models/quantizations, 3) throughput vs cost curves for reserved vs burst. short caption per panel.

sahil: can eng confirm the benchmark numbers? i can pull the perf run but want to be careful about lab vs prod caveats.

mara: flagged for eng verification. also want a small narrative: "how to read the plot" and a one-liner for the launch post.

kim: For the one-liner — something like: "Ship LLM features without surprise bills: predictable latency and unit economics across deployments." short & punchy.

jen: nit: mention fallbacks/variants so enterprise readers see reliability angle. e.g., "automatic fallbacks keep latency SLOs intact when capacity shifts."

alex: agree. also we should sketch headline variants for AB test: A) Predictable latency, predictable cost; B) Same API, lower surprise; C) SLA-ready inference economics.

mara: good. next: visuals — who can do quick mockups? kim can you or design?

kim: can do rough wireframes today. i need these assets from eng: numbers + sample latency distributions for hosted vs dedicated vs private. ideally a CSV with: model, deployment, p50,p95,p99, tokens_per_1k_cost, throughput_rps.

sahil: i'll export the latest runs from perf infra but will add a lab vs prod note. expected ETA: EOD tomorrow. sample rows:
```# model,deployment,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,throughput_rps
redwood-1-small,hosted,45,120,320,0.28,120
redwood-1-small,dedicated,40,90,150,0.25,900
open-approx-quant,hosted,50,160,420,0.18,140
```

mara: perfect. design can mock off that.

alex: for the cost panel, let's add a small annotation calling out quantization wins vs cache/batching wins. people love concrete callouts.

jen: inbound routing: what happens after we publish? we should route enterprise-type queries (mentions SLA, private) to AE queue; product interest to growth. i can map rules.

mara: yes — suggested routing rules: if message contains "SLA" or "private" or "HSM" -> route to enterprise-sales; if contains "pilot" or "dedicated" -> AE follow-up; general interest -> marketing nurture. add UTM so we can track.

jen: I'll create a simple playbook. do we want a gated webinar for enterprise leads or an on-demand recording?

kim: hybrid: gated webinar for enterprise track (invite via AE) + recording & short snackable for PLG funnel. webinar CTA in launch post should be "See a live comparison + ask our engs".

alex: timeline check: perf numbers EOD tomorrow, design mockups two days, copy + landing page by Friday, webinar signup page + routing live next Tue?

mara: that works. i'll own the launch post copy and the three slide visuals.

ops-bot: deploy reminder — marketing site slot available Wed 09:00 UTC.

sahil: quick flag — include an explicit note in the copy: "numbers reflect tested config; real app performance depends on prompt length, batch size, and cache usage." keeps us honest.

mara: yes. add small methods blurb below visuals: hardware, seq len distribution, batching strategy.

jen: i'll draft routing rules and draft AE playbook. will ping ops for integration (Slack -> CRM).

kim: will mock two visual styles: narrative-first (big claim + simple plots) and data-first (detailed table + small plots). want to test which converts.

alex: FYI let's prepare two headline CTA strings + two hero images for AB.

mara: final asks: eng perf CSV, design mockups, a 50–70 char punchline, and webinar gating plan. owners: sahil, kim, mara, jen.

jen: acknowledged. i'll post routing doc in #marketing-playbooks when ready.

sahil: adding a note — we should retest after quantization updates next week; may shift numbers slightly.

mara: ok. thanks all — i'll assemble a draft post once mockups come in. :thumbsup:
